title: adaptive priority sampler for smoke evals + CI hook
author: Nina Park
release_notes: Adds an adaptive sampling hook for smoke evaluations to prioritize underperforming cohorts and reduce CI cost. Non-breaking. Defaults disabled; opt-in via config.
description:
Motivation: Our smoke CI runs are dominated by stable cohorts and waste budget repeating low-signal prompts. This PR adds an adaptive priority sampler and a lightweight CI hook that biases selection toward cohorts with recent regression signal or high variance. Goals: 1) improve early detection of prompt-set regressions by increasing sampling density on fragile cohorts; 2) reduce average cost of smoke runs while maintaining coverage; 3) provide observability for why a cohort was sampled.

What this PR does: Adds an AdaptivePrioritySampler that uses a simple score = alpha * recent_regression_score + beta * variance_score + gamma * recency_boost, where weights are configurable. Integrates sampler as a CI hook (smoke_priority_sampler) that can be inserted into existing smoke pipelines; provides a replay-friendly seed for deterministic runs in CI. Includes: - sampler implementation and unit tests - CI adapter that emits selection telemetry and decision reasons to the smoke run trace - a small migration to add "priority_score" metadata to cohort manifests - docs for enabling and tuning the hook in the smoke CI job config (example included).

Checklist: [x] unit tests added for sampler logic and config parsing; [x] integration test for CI adapter simulating skewed cohort scores; [x] docs for ops + example smoke job snippet; [ ] e2e in staging smoke pipeline (follow-up, tracked ENG-4310).

Usage (short): Add smoke_priority_sampler to the smoke job's hooks list and set sampler.config.weights to tune. Default config is conservative (alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1) and the hook is opt-in.

Related: ENG-4281 (smoke CI cost reduction), SUP-3421 (support ticket requesting more targeted regression checks).

Commits (summary): - 8f3c2b1: initial sampler and basic config parsing - b2d4ae5: hook adapter + telemetry emission - c14f7a0: tests for edge cases, deterministic seed handling - d9a8b21: docs and example pipeline snippet - e6f3c93: tweak default weights after perf review

Changed areas (high level): - eval_harness/samplers/priority_sampler.py (core logic, ~220 LOC) - eval_harness/ci/hooks/smoke_priority_hook.py (adapter) - eval_harness/tests/test_priority_sampler.py (unit tests) - docs/ci/smoke_priority_sampler.md (usage) - eval_harness/manifests/cohorts_v2.yaml (added optional priority metadata) - internal/tools/ci_templates/smoke_job.yaml (example insertion)

Small illustrative snippet (sampler scoring):
score = (alpha * regression_score) + (beta * variance_score) + (gamma * recency_boost)
# deterministic seed: seed = hash(run_id + job_name) % (2**32)

CI run notes: First CI run failed lint on one minor import order and a flake8 max-line-length breach; fixed in b2d4ae5. Integration test initially flaky due to nondeterministic timestamp in recency_boost; added a fixed-time override in tests. Final CI: all checks green.

Why unique: Prior approaches (cohort reweighting) adjusted post-hoc; this sampler makes selection bias explicit and reproducible, plus it outputs a reason string per sampled cohort which helps triage blips in eval dashboards.

Risks & mitigations: Over-biasing could starve cold cohorts — mitigated by a floor probability per cohort and a configurable entropy cap. Performance: sampler is O(N) on cohort list and runs in <20ms for typical smoke sizes.

Next steps: rollout to staging smoke pipeline (ENG-4310), monitor detection rate and CI cost delta for two weeks, and iterate on default weights.
